\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Profile Approximation}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.ProfileApproximation
\section{Overview}
Continuity and vanishing endpoint values control the Gaussian profile by distance to either endpoint probability. Consequently, Gaussian averaging of a measurable indicator has an integral profile tending to zero.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Profile bound by distance to endpoints]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile_endpoint_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile_nonneg,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuousOn_closedGaussianProfile}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Phi,\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and let $\overline I(p)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$, with $\overline I(p)=0$ elsewhere. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $C>0$ such that $\overline I(p)\le\varepsilon+C|p-b|$ for all $p\in[0,1]$ and $b\in\{0,1\}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integral profile bounded by rotation sensitivity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_profile_averagedGaussianIndicator_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator_mem_unitInterval,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile_endpoint_bound,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile_nonneg,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_averagedGaussianIndicator,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_abs_averagedGaussianIndicator_sub_indicator,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Phi,\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and let $\overline I(p)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$, with $\overline I(p)=0$ elsewhere. Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For a measurable $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, let $u_\theta(x)=\mathbb E_Y1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,Y)$ with $Y\sim\gamma_n$, and put $R_A(\theta)=\Pr(1_A(X)\ne1_A(\cos\theta\,X+\sin\theta\,Y))$ for independent $X,Y\sim\gamma_n$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $C>0$ such that $\int\overline I(u_\theta(x))\,d\gamma_n(x)\le\varepsilon+CR_A(\theta)$ for every real $\theta$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Vanishing integral profile of averaged indicators]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_integral_profile_averagedGaussianIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile_nonneg,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_profile_averagedGaussianIndicator_le,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_tendsto_zero,BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Phi,\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and let $\overline I(p)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$, with $\overline I(p)=0$ elsewhere. Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For a measurable $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, let $u_\theta(x)=\mathbb E_Y1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,Y)$ with $Y\sim\gamma_n$, and put $R_A(\theta)=\Pr(1_A(X)\ne1_A(\cos\theta\,X+\sin\theta\,Y))$ for independent $X,Y\sim\gamma_n$. Then $\int\overline I(u_\theta(x))\,d\gamma_n(x)\to0$ as $\theta\to0$ through real values.
\end{lemma}
